newsitem.title: USA: Calif. agency says 25,000 cows displaced by floods.
newsitem.headline: Calif. agency says 25,000 cows displaced by floods.

text.p: Up to 200,000 acres of land have been inundated and about 25,000 cows displaced by floods hitting California, according to estimates quoted by the state Department of Food and Agriculture on Thursday.

Heavy rainstorms have caused severe floods in parts of central and northern California over the last week, damaging hundreds of homes and putting wide areas of farmland under water in the state's fertile central valley.
Official estimates of damage to homes, businesses and infrastructure have already passed $1.5 billion, but no estimate of agricultural losses has yet been released in America's No. 1 farming state.

In a flood relief update issued on Thursday, the California Department of Food and Agriculture said it continued to work with the U.S. Department of Agriculture and local agricultural commissioners on an initial damage report.

However, the department said Western United Dairyman, a dairy industry organisation, had estimated that about 25,000 cows had been displaced by the floods. It said other state agencies estimated that between 150,000 and 200,000 acres of land had been flooded throughout the state.

The agricultural commissioner of Yuba County, north of Sacramento, reported that some prune and walnut dehydrator facilities were completely under water, the department said. Several cases of apples and pears being held in cold storage were inundated, it said.
The department said about 23 dairies statewide had been affected so far by flooding.
A dairy operation with 350 dairy cows in Yuba County had been flooded and about 200 cows were lost, it said.

It said initial reports were that 15 dairy farms in San Joaquin County in central California had been evacuated and relocated and about four others were threatened. Three dairies had been relocated in nearby Stanislaus County.

The areas between the Tuolumne and San Joaquin rivers in central California were hardest hit with numerous dairy operations flooded, it said. This region produces about 37 percent of California's total milk production, it added.
